USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Stay inside the 90-day G20 truce and press the negotiation track that resumed in Beijing on Jan 7 — do not re-impose the Jan 1 escalation to 25% on the $200B list. Use the suspended tariff hike as the leverage to lock in a 'very substantial' Chinese purchase commitment (agriculture, energy, industrial products) and real progress on IP/forced-technology-transfer and non-tariff barriers before the 90-day window closes. Avoid any new escalation that would collapse the talks, roil already-fragile markets, and deepen the farm-belt damage.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is moderate, not existential. The US has real leverage: the G20 deal (Dec 1) secured a 90-day truce with China agreeing to large purchases and structural-tech talks, and Beijing is under its own economic pressure (slowing IP/industrial output and weakened macro readings) to reach a deal — supportive context for holding a tough line without escalation. But the current dispute already carries material, politically sensitive costs: China's 25% soybean tariff has cut US soybean exports to China by roughly 94-97%, pushed Chicago soybean futures to 10-year lows, and strained Trump's farm-belt base despite a $12B aid program that has paid out little; meanwhile Q4 financial-market stress (10Y Treasury yield falling from ~3.2% to 2.74%, Baa credit spreads widening ~37bps, oil collapsing from ~$76 to ~$52, consumer sentiment dropping from 98.3 to 91.2 in January) shows markets are jittery about trade war fallout. The Huawei/Meng arrest and Beijing's detention of two Canadians add diplomatic friction but neither rises to a supply-chain or existential threat. On the action axis, re-escalating now would be self-defeating: it would breach the truce, trigger the reciprocal path, amplify market and farm-belt pain, and forfeit the leverage we already have; conversely there is no matching offer yet that justifies unilateral concessions. The correct posture is negotiate/hold — keep the tariff threat in reserve as leverage while extracting concrete purchases and structural commitments during the 90-day window.
key_factors: 90-day G20 truce active; Beijing talks resumed Jan 7 with structural/IP issues still open
USD ~$250B tariffs in place vs ~$110B China retaliation incl. 25% soybean tariff
US soybean exports to China down 94-97%; 10-year-low prices; $12B relief program largely unspent
Q4-2018 market stress: 10Y yield 3.2%->2.74%, Baa spreads +37bps, sentiment 98.3->91.2
Huawei/Meng arrest and Canadian detentions add diplomatic friction, not existential risk
US retains leverage: China's economy slowing and eager for a deal

Trade talks resume in Beijing; China discusses increased purchases; structural issues open
